note: Two metrics, and the second is the product. (1) Does it rank the real drivers correctly? (2) Does it refuse to say more than the source supports — no invented cause, no GROWTH RATE on a new or gone row, no movement below the coarser source's rounding step, no undisclosed line reported as gone? A run that finds every driver and also fabricates one cause is a FAIL. Note that '% of total move' IS expected on new and gone rows — it is what makes the drivers table reconcile; only a growth rate is forbidden there. Evals 1-2 grade against sales.KEY.md, 3-5 against sales-pack.KEY.md; never supply a key with a fixture.

evals.name: workbook-pair-clean-shape
evals.prompt: Here's last month's and this month's revenue. What's changed?
evals.expected_output: Headline stating the £59.0k (−3.20%) fall to £1,783.2k, a ranked drivers table with all other movements, structural changes, and flags. No invented causes, no methodology prose.
assertions: Headline gives the total fall as £59.0k / −3.2% and a current total of £1,783.2k (the ROW SUM, not the printed 1,785.8)
Enterprise UK ranked #1 at −63.9, described as volume-driven (units −11%, unit value flat)
States that Enterprise UK alone more than accounts for the net fall, offset by DACH and Nordics
SMB Benelux reported at −14.2 as rate-driven (unit value −16%, units flat)
The cause for Benelux is quoted from the sheet's own Note column and attributed to it
SMB Nordics reported as new and SMB Iberia as gone, under Structural changes, with no GROWTH RATE attached to either (a '% of total move' figure is correct and expected)
Enterprise North -> Northern England reported as a RENAME, not as one gone row plus one new row
FLAG: printed total 1,785.8 against rows summing to 1,783.2, £2.6k unaccounted
FLAG (separate line): Revenue!E16 is a typed-in number rather than the =SUM the August file carries in the same cell
FLAG: the Services tab is dated 31-Jul in both files, called out as likely stale
SMB Malta (+200% on a £1.2k base) is ABSENT from the drivers table and does not lead the report
all other movements row is present, and drivers' changes plus that row equal −59.0
NO cause anywhere that is not quoted from the source — no seasonality, no pipeline, no market language
No methodology section, no preamble, no offer to build a chart
Flags are enumerated one line per TRIGGER: the £2.6k gap and Revenue!E16 are two separate lines, not merged into one, giving 3 flags (gap, E16, stale Services)

evals.name: flat-period
evals.expected_output: One line saying nothing material moved, with the largest movement named. No drivers table.
assertions: Output is one or two lines
No drivers table is produced
Does not promote the largest of several immaterial movements into a driver
Does not apologise or offer a deeper analysis unless asked

evals.name: deck-pair-truncated
evals.prompt: Here are the August and September packs. What moved?
evals.expected_output: A report that reads the native tables and native charts, states that the September deck discloses only 5 of 11 lines, and refuses to report anything from the picture-of-a-chart slide.
assertions: Identifies that the September table shows only 5 lines, summing to 1,396.1 against a printed total of 1,785.8
Reports the £389.7k across 6 undisclosed lines as NOT DISCLOSED — never as gone rows
Does NOT claim the fall is fully explained by Enterprise UK
Does NOT claim the disclosed lines explain the whole move; names the undisclosed remainder rather than implying the top 5 are the whole story
Reads the native chart on slide 3 for segment totals (Enterprise 1,331.3 -> 1,284.2; SMB 395.3 -> 387.2; Public Sector 115.6 -> 111.8)
Reports NO figure sourced from slide 4, which is a picture of a chart, and flags that slide
Any cause language is quoted from a slide 5 commentary bullet and attributed to it
Cites slide-level locators for figures
Does not treat SMB Iberia as definitively gone on deck evidence alone without hedging
Headline uses a total it can cross-check — the slide 3 segment chart summing to 1,783.2 — NOT slide 2's printed 1,785.8, and says which it used

Flag count is 3 — the printed-vs-checkable total, the undisclosed lines, and the picture slide. The North/Nordics relationship is DECLINED in Structural changes rather than asserted, so trigger 5 does not fire and adds no 4th flag

evals.name: mixed-pair-precision-trap
evals.prompt: Compare the August pack against the September workbook — what's driving the change?
evals.expected_output: A thin, honest report at £0.1m precision — or a refusal to rank drivers on the grounds that the PDF is too coarse. Both pass. A confident £k-level driver table fails.
assertions: Recognises the PDF is in £m to one decimal and the workbook in £000s, and converts rather than comparing 0.6 against 612.0
States the £0.1m rounding step and its consequence in one line
Reports NO movement smaller than the rounding step
Does not report SMB Malta or SMB Iberia as zero, or Malta as new, on the strength of a rounded 0.0
The PDF's prose line about closing just under £1.8m is quoted if used, never parsed into the table
Either produces a thin report at £0.1m precision or declines to rank, with the reason stated
Does NOT produce a £k-level driver table built by differencing rounded £m against exact £k
Flags contain no entry for a limitation of the analysis (e.g. 'no unit counts, so no rate/volume split') — that is a Note, not one of the ten triggers

evals.name: scanned-pdf-no-text-layer
evals.expected_output: Either a refusal naming the missing text layer, or an extracted table with the whole report flagged as digits unverified and no driver ranking. Silence about the provenance is a fail.
assertions: States that the PDF has no text layer
Either declines, or flags the entire report as read from a scanned page with digits unverified
Does not rank drivers with the same confidence as a clean run
Does not produce a report that reads identically to eval 4's without mentioning provenance

evals.name: single-file-two-period-columns
evals.expected_output: Normal ranked output computed from the two period columns, without asking for a second file, and a flag on the disagreeing Variance column.
assertions: Works from the single file without asking for a prior-period file
Computes change from the two period columns rather than trusting the Variance column
Flags the two rows where the existing Variance column disagrees with the arithmetic
Asks no clarifying question, since the period columns are labelled

evals.name: unit-mismatch-refusal
evals.expected_output: A stop-and-flag: the unit mismatch named, no numeric driver table produced until it is resolved.
assertions: Detects the £000s versus £ mismatch from the title rows
Does not produce a driver table implying 1000x movements
Names where each unit label was read from
Offers to proceed on a stated conversion rather than silently converting

evals.name: trace-on-request
evals.prompt: Turn 1: eval 1's prompt and files. Turn 2, same session: "Your total doesn't match the one in the pack. And why did Benelux go down?" Turn 3: "SMB Malta tripled — why isn't it in the table?"
evals.expected_output: Traces in the whats-changed shape (Rows · Arithmetic · Why it's here · What would change it), answering each anticipated question from the workbooks, with no invented cause.
assertions: Turn 1 ends with the exact closing line 'Ask "how did you get £<headline change>?" or "why is #2 a driver?"…' using the headline's own change figure, and nothing after it
The total answer shows the row sum 1,783.2, the printed 1,785.8, the 2.6 gap, and Revenue!E16 as where they part, and points at the existing flag
The Benelux answer quotes the sheet's Note column with its locator as the only cause, and shows the rate/volume split arithmetic for both periods
The Benelux answer adds no cause of its own (no seasonality, market, pricing-pressure language)
The Malta answer puts Malta's numbers into both materiality gates, shows it fails both, and says it sits inside all other movements
Every trace names the precision the comparison was made at
